description: We are Hack the Future, a team of enthusiastic beginners eager to explore space, technology, and innovation. Though we are still learning, we believe in creativity, teamwork, and solving real-world problems. We welcome curious and passionate participants who are interested in coding, AI/ML, data analysis, web development, design, or science. Let's learn, build, and innovate together!
summary: We built Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer to make learning about space feel more like an adventure. It takes young learners through themed missions about rockets, the Moon, Mars, the International Space Station and more. In each mission, they explore a short briefing, answer space science questions and see how their progress grows through points, stars and new mission unlocks. There is also a rocket racing mini-game where players dodge asteroids and collect energy crystals. We hope the project gives children a fun, welcoming way to explore space science and encourages them to stay curious about the universe.
details: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser-based learning project for children aged 7–14. We wanted to make space science feel more engaging than reading facts on a page, so we organized the experience around astronaut missions. Learners can explore topics such as rockets, the Moon, Mars, the International Space Station and the solar system through short briefings and multiple-choice quizzes. Each mission has 20 questions; correct answers earn points, and learners can track their progress and unlock the next mission by passing. The project also includes a rocket racing mini-game where players dodge asteroids and collect energy crystals. We built the experience with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, including the mission content, quiz flow, scoring and progress features. Our goal is to encourage curiosity and make space learning approachable for young explorers.
